document.title: Afghanistan: Military Situation Reviewed (Peshaw 00021)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Reviews Taliban military gains in 2000 and the issues facing the Taliban and Massoud's opposition. The Taliban's summer offensive failed with heavy casualties, and their only success is on the battlefield. Uzbekistan-Taliban accommodation threatens Massoud's supply lines. Dostum's possible alliance with Massoud is unclear. Excised.

key_claims: The Taliban made significant gains north of the Hindu Kush in 2000, notably taking Taloqan, but cannot deliver a knock-out blow.
The Northern Alliance's future depends on Ahmad Shah Masoud's leadership and his ability to procure materiel.
Taliban operations in the Shomali are directed by the Ministry of Defense in Kabul and staged from Shakar Dara, Ghorband and Nijrab.
Pashtun tribesmen in Khost remain restive and undisarmed, but are unlikely to ally with the Tajik-dominated UIFSA.
Qari Ahmadullah's deployment to both Takhar and Bamiyan may signal his rising importance in the Taliban.
Dostum and Ismail Khan cannot return in a major way without Uzbek/Iranian support; Tajikistan blocks Dostum's use of its territory.
Taliban control about 95 percent of Afghanistan but lack capacity beyond fighting.
Masoud's supply lines are threatened by growing Uzbekistan-Taliban accommodation.
Taliban blockade of Panjshir caused a tenfold rise in food prices.
Ismail Khan and Dostum cannot return without Iranian and Uzbek support, which is unlikely.
Source believes Pakistan was supplying the Taliban ahead of UNSCR 1333 sanctions.
